analysis.title: NFP, France, and Diesel - GS Daily Monitor
key_insights: Nonfarm payrolls came in at +29k, well below estimates, and the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2%. Payrolls for the prior two months were revised down.

France proposed that European countries and International Energy Agency (IEA) members release diesel and crude oil from reserves. The proposal is 50 million barrels of diesel from European countries and 50 million barrels of crude from IEA members.
The OAT-Bund spread (French 10-year yield minus German) widened past 130bps, with spillover into Italian BTPs. GS reads this as political risk premium building in French bonds.
Korea's finance minister said after the F4 meeting that treasury bond issuance may be cut further if needed.
Thai exports are getting a boost from AI-driven demand, but 70% of the inputs are sourced overseas.
The Romanian central bank let the RON weaken 1.7% against the EUR.
The IMF confirmed that Senegal's authorities have met with bilateral creditors.

Chart of the Day: the OAT-Bund spread has jumped past 130bps in recent sessions as French bonds face structural challenges from rising debt concerns. French elections are upcoming, and EURUSD skew has shifted notably.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Well below estimates, with downward revisions to the prior two months. Points to a weakening labor market.
The rate ticked up, consistent with a softer labor market.
